pages.class_justification: Proven complexity-class containment; the reduction-class axis does not discriminate, per repo convention for inclusions.
pages.model_justification: The containment IP ⊆ PSPACE is unconditional and unrelativized; the CCG+94 random-oracle separation is a different (barrier-type) statement and must not set this page's model.
pages.statement: $\classIP \subseteq \classPSPACE$: for every [[interactive-proof-systems|IP]] verifier, the maximum acceptance probability over all prover strategies is computable in [[polynomial-space|PSPACE]] by recursion over the interaction tree — folklore.
pages.sketch: Fix the verifier. The optimal acceptance probability of a partial transcript is the maximum over the prover's next message at prover moves and the average over the verifier's coins at verifier moves. Depth-first evaluation of this recursion over the polynomial-depth interaction tree uses polynomial space; accept iff the value at the root is at least $2/3$.
notes_to_keep: The relativized separation $\classIP^A \neq \classPSPACE^A$ for a random oracle $A$ ([[CCG+94 - The random oracle hypothesis is false|CCG+94]]) is a distinct statement, recorded at [[no-rom-to-roh-ccg-94]]; it does not bear on the unrelativized containment.

The source field should become folklore; the CCG+94 wikilink should be dropped from this page.

pages.statement: $\classIP \subseteq \classQIP$: a classical [[interactive-proof-systems|IP]] protocol is a [[quantum-interactive-proofs|QIP]] protocol whose verifier measures each incoming message in the computational basis and otherwise runs the classical verifier — folklore.
pages.sketch: Measuring each prover message in the computational basis turns any quantum prover into a randomized classical prover: the distribution of each message given the classical transcript so far is a classical strategy. Completeness and soundness of the classical protocol carry over unchanged.

pages.wrong_reason: The Fiat–Shamir transform removes interaction from public-coin protocols; it does not create succinctness. Applied to a general interactive proof it yields a non-interactive argument whose length equals the original communication, so no SNARK results unless the protocol is already succinct. The ROM edges that do hold are PCP + ROM ⇒ SNARG (Micali, CS proofs, FOCS 1994 / SICOMP 30(4), 2000) and public-coin IOP + ROM ⇒ SNARK (Ben-Sasson–Chiesa–Spooner, TCC 2016-B), the latter via state-restoration soundness for many-round protocols. FS86 is an identification/signature paper with no statement about succinct arguments.
flags: The sibling page content/Reductions/interactive-protocol-and-rom-to-snark.md (batch red-15) carries the same defective claim; fix them consistently.

Replacement edges would need new hypothesis objects and reference stubs: Mic00 (Micali, 'Computationally Sound Proofs', SICOMP 2000) and BCS16 (Ben-Sasson, Chiesa, Spooner, 'Interactive Oracle Proofs', TCC 2016-B); neither is in content/References/ yet.
Even for public-coin protocols, multi-round Fiat–Shamir needs round-by-round / state-restoration soundness — any corrected page must carry that qualifier.
verifier_changes: wrong_reason: tightened wording; claim verified as wrong (FS preserves communication, gives no succinctness); Micali FOCS 94 and BCS16 TCC 2016-B bibliographic data confirmed against cryptobib

pages.wrong_reason: Not a theorem: SZK ⊆ AM ∩ coAM (Fortnow 1987; Aiello–Håstad 1991), so IP ⊆ SZK together with IP = PSPACE would give PSPACE ⊆ AM ∩ coAM and collapse the polynomial hierarchy. BGG+90 prove that, assuming a secure probabilistic encryption scheme (one-way functions suffice by later work), every language in IP has a COMPUTATIONAL zero-knowledge proof; the migrated bullet dropped that hypothesis and upgraded computational to statistical zero knowledge. The intended BGG+90 content is the conjunctive edge {ip, hash-function (OWF)} ⇒ czk, and the wiki already carries czk-to-ip-bgg-90 ('CZK = IP').

sources.ref_file_title: KSW08 - Predicate Encryption Supporting Disjunctions Polynomial Equations and Inner Products
sources.authors: Jonathan Katz, Amit Sahai, Brent Waters
sources.note: Applications section shows inner-product predicate encryption implies HVE (and anonymous IBE, disjunctions, polynomial evaluation, CNF/DNF).

pages.class_justification: The construction uses the IPPE scheme only as an oracle, but the generic security argument is not clean: with the coefficients $r_i$ in the key, an adversary that recovers them from an IPPE key (attribute-hiding constrains ciphertexts, not keys; a scheme may append the key vector in the clear) can choose a non-matching challenge attribute with zero inner product — trivial when $\Sigma = \ZZ_p$ — which is admissible in the HVE game but inadmissible in the IPPE game. A fully-black-box reduction therefore needs an extra hypothesis (the encoded key vector is hidden, or HVE security is selective). KSW08 do not classify the reduction; left unstated.
pages.model_justification: Generic encoding-based transformation; no idealized model.
pages.statement: An attribute-hiding [[inner-product-predicate-encryption|IPPE]] scheme of dimension $2n$ over $\ZZ_p$ yields an [[hidden-vector-encryption|HVE]] scheme for patterns in $(\Sigma \cup \{*\})^n$ with $\Sigma \subseteq \ZZ_p$: a pattern $v$ with wildcard set $S$ and an attribute $x$ are encoded as vectors whose inner product is $\sum_{i \notin S} r_i (x_i - v_i)$ for uniformly random coefficients $r_i$, which vanishes when $v$ matches $x$ and otherwise with probability $1/p$. Attribute-hiding transfers whenever an HVE adversary's encoded queries stay admissible in the IPPE game, i.e. unless it finds a non-matching attribute whose encoded inner product vanishes — [[KSW08 - Predicate Encryption Supporting Disjunctions Polynomial Equations and Inner Products|KSW08]].
pages.sketch: Encode $x$ as $(x_1, 1, \ldots, x_n, 1)$ and $v$ as $(r_1, -r_1 v_1, \ldots, r_n, -r_n v_n)$ with $r_i = 0$ for $i \in S$ and $r_i \getsr \ZZ_p$ otherwise, sampled at key generation; $\Setup$, $\KeyGen$, $\Enc$, $\Dec$ of the HVE scheme call the IPPE algorithms once each on the encoded vectors.
flags: CLASS DOWNGRADED fully-black-box → unstated: the encoded HVE adversary can violate IPPE admissibility by targeting the key-side randomness (see class_justification). The bad event is negligible when the $r_i$ are hidden from the adversary (as in KSW08's own scheme, where they sit in exponents) or when the coefficients are moved to the ciphertext; a human should check KSW08 §5 for how the paper handles this before any class is recorded.

Sketch follows KSW08's key-side randomization (coefficients chosen at key generation); the encoding identity $\sum_{i \notin S} r_i (x_i - v_i)$ is certain, the side carrying the randomness should be confirmed against KSW08 §5 (web access unavailable during verification).

KSW08's own IPPE instantiation works over $\ZZ_N$ for composite $N$; the encoding is stated here over prime $\ZZ_p$ to match the wiki's IPPE syntax, giving false-accept probability exactly $1/p$ per non-matching (key, ciphertext) pair.
The randomized-coefficient point from the migration notes (a deterministic embedding would create false accepts) is carried by the statement.
verifier_changes: class fully-black-box → unstated: the security reduction is not generically admissibility-preserving (adversary can target key-side coefficients); justification rewritten
statement: dimension $O(n)$ → $2n$ (KSW08 use $2\ell$); added the admissibility condition under which attribute-hiding transfers; tightened
sketch: rewritten to the encoding only; removed 'forwards them to the IPPE game unchanged', which glossed over the admissibility failure
sources: KSW08 kept (EUROCRYPT 2008, DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-78967-3_9 confirmed against cryptobib; HVE application is in KSW08 §5)
flags: rewritten to record the downgrade reason and the open check

sources.ref_file_title: KSW08 - Predicate Encryption Supporting Disjunctions Polynomial Equations and Inner Products
sources.authors: Jonathan Katz, Amit Sahai, Brent Waters
sources.note: Defines payload-hiding and attribute-hiding and names the latter as the stronger notion; the implication itself is immediate.

pages.class_justification: Identity construction; the reduction forwards a payload-hiding adversary verbatim into the attribute-hiding game with $x_0 = x_1 = x^*$. Both construction and reduction are fixed and treat scheme and adversary as oracles.
pages.statement: An attribute-hiding [[inner-product-predicate-encryption|IPPE]] scheme is [[inner-product-predicate-encryption#payload-only-hiding|payload-hiding]]: a payload-hiding adversary with challenge $(x^*, m_0), (x^*, m_1)$ is an admissible attribute-hiding adversary with $x_0 = x_1 = x^*$, since $\langle v, x_0 \rangle = 0 \Leftrightarrow \langle v, x_1 \rangle = 0$ holds for every $v$ — folklore.
pages.sketch: The payload-hiding game is the attribute-hiding game restricted to challenges with equal attribute vectors; the reduction is the identity on scheme and adversary and preserves the advantage exactly.
pages.improvements_text: - Payload-hiding and attribute-hiding, the latter the stronger notion, are defined in [[KSW08 - Predicate Encryption Supporting Disjunctions Polynomial Equations and Inner Products|KSW08]].
flags: The conclusion is a Variations-section anchor (payload-hiding-ippe), not a standalone page; fine as recorded.

PRIMITIVE-PAGE DEFECT (skeptical-checker lane, not this edge): the attribute-hiding game on inner-product-predicate-encryption.md omits KSW08's second admissibility condition — if $\langle v, x_0 \rangle = \langle v, x_1 \rangle = 0$ for some queried $v$ then $m_0 = m_1$. Without it the game is trivially won with $x_0 = x_1$ and one matching key query. hidden-vector-encryption.md has the same omission. The payload-hiding adversary never queries a matching $v$, so this edge holds under either version.

pages.class_justification: Identity construction, using the IT-PIR scheme only as an oracle. Any efficient distinguisher between per-server query distributions has advantage bounded by their statistical distance, which is zero for an IT-PIR; the reduction forwards the adversary unchanged.
pages.statement: Every [[multi-server-private-information-retrieval|IT-PIR]] scheme is a [[multi-server-private-information-retrieval#computational-multi-server-pir|computational multi-server PIR]]: per-server query distributions that are identical for every pair of indices are in particular computationally indistinguishable — folklore.

pages.class_justification: The construction invokes the two-party protocol only as an oracle (one independent session per party); the hybrid security reduction runs any multi-party eavesdropper as an oracle, embedding the two-party challenge into one session and simulating the remaining sessions itself.
pages.statement: Two-party [[key-exchange|KE]] implies [[key-exchange#multi-party-key-exchange|multi-party key exchange]] against eavesdroppers: a designated party runs an independent KE session with each of the other $n-1$ parties, samples a group key $K$ uniformly, and sends $K$ one-time-padded under each session key — folklore.
pages.sketch: A hybrid over the $n-1$ sessions replaces each session key by an independent uniform key using two-party KE security; the reduction embeds its challenge in one session and generates the others itself. In the final hybrid every pad is uniform and independent of $K$, so $K$ is independent of the transcript.
pages.security_loss: factor $n-1$ over the two-party KE advantage (one hybrid per session)
flags: The multi-party KE subsection on key-exchange.md has no formal security game; the generic construction above achieves eavesdropper (passive) security matching the two-party notion the page defines. If a stronger multi-party notion is ever formalized there, this edge must be rechecked.

Burmester–Desmedt (EUROCRYPT '94) and Joux's tripartite pairing protocol, named in the migrated text, are constant-round constructions from specific assumptions (DDH, pairings) — they are efficiency improvements under different hypotheses, not sources for this generic edge, and would need their own reduction pages and reference stubs.
The generic construction costs one extra round of communication after the pairwise sessions; 'requires additional rounds or structure' in the migrated text refers to avoiding that cost.

pages.wrong_reason: Unsupported as stated: the wiki's KE object is a general interactive protocol, and an arbitrary multi-round KE gives no way to encrypt in a single message under a reusable public key; whether general KE implies PKE is open. The folklore edge is 2-message KE ⇒ PKE: the initiator's first message is the public key, Enc runs the responder and one-time-pads the plaintext with the session key, Dec recomputes the key from the initiator's state; a hybrid over responder sessions handles public-key reuse. The one-time pad makes the migrated parenthetical's symmetric-cipher hypothesis unnecessary for messages up to the key length. DH76 introduces key exchange but proves no such theorem; ElGamal85 instantiates the transformation for the Diffie–Hellman protocol.
flags: A corrected page needs a 2-message-KE (or NIKE, anchor key-exchange#non-interactive-key-exchange-nike) hypothesis object; none exists as a slug, so the fix is blocked on the object level. The converse page pke-to-ke.md (batch red-24) is unaffected: PKE ⇒ 2-message KE is fine.
Whether general interactive KE implies PKE is open; the page must not be re-sourced with the current hypothesis.

If retargeted to NIKE ⇒ PKE, [[ElGamal85 - A Public Key Cryptosystem and a Signature Scheme Based on Discrete Logarithms|ElGamal85]] (already in content/References/) is the natural instantiation citation, with the generic statement still folklore.
